exposure: Initial diagnosis of first-onset severe mental illness (SMI) during the postpartum period
Timing of symptom onset (within first 6 months post-delivery)
cohort: The study included 120 women admitted to a mother-baby unit for first-onset severe mental illness during the first six months following delivery.
finding: Women with first-onset Acute Transient Psychotic Disorder (ATPD) have a higher chance of recurrence and conversion to bipolar disorder, while those initially diagnosed with severe depressive episode or unspecified non-organic psychosis tend to maintain their diagnosis over time, with the first 12 weeks post-delivery identified as a vulnerable period for first-onset SMI.
